summary_html: Youth remains in **extended foster care** or receives **transitional services** after age 18 under federal programs promoting independence.
authority_html:

- **FCSIAA** — extends care to age 21 with education and housing supports

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Third District
key_cases.holding: Dismissal of a private dependency petition filed two days before the youth turned eighteen was affirmed because the record supported the finding that he had not been abandoned, abused or neglected by his mother.
key_cases.relevance: A petition filed on the eve of the youth's eighteenth birthday cannot substitute for statutory dependency grounds.
key_cases.quote: we agree that S.A.R.D. failed to establish that he is a dependent child under Chapter 39, Florida Statutes (2015)

key_cases.case_name: E.G. v. Department of Children & Families
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Third District
key_cases.holding: Certiorari was granted quashing an order that directed a dependent minor to 'voluntarily' enter residential drug treatment and to abstain from running away, because the trial court lacked authority to compel that placement.
key_cases.relevance: The order also purported to restrain an older foster youth from running away, and the court held that exceeded its authority.
key_cases.quote: we agree with the Minor that the trial court lacked the authority to direct him to "voluntarily submit himself" to the residential treatment facility
